questions.prompt: What makes a software project **open source** under the OSI definition?

options.text: Source code is publicly available under an OSI-approved license granting rights to use, inspect, modify, and redistribute
It is freeware with hidden source code

questions.prompt: Match each open-source license family to its key obligation.

columns.label: Allows proprietary/commercial redistribution with attribution and license notice
Derivative works distributed externally must also be licensed under GPLv3
Modifications to the library itself stay LGPL, while applications linking it may use any license

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a `CONTRIBUTING.md` file in a repository?

options.text: Explaining how to set up dev/test tools, coding conventions, and how to submit pull requests

questions.prompt: Which community health files belong in a well-maintained open-source repository? (Select all that apply.)
In **Git**, what is a **fork-and-pull-request** workflow?

options.text: Pushing directly to `main` on someone else's repo
Cloning a personal fork, committing on a feature branch, and opening a PR back to upstream

code.source:
git checkout -b fix/typo-docs
git push -u origin fix/typo-docs

questions.prompt: Why should contributors **avoid working directly on `main`** in their fork?

options.text: Keeping `main` clean to mirror upstream lets you open multiple independent PRs from separate topic branches

questions.prompt: What makes a **commit message** useful during `git log` or `git bisect`?

options.text: A concise imperative subject describing what changed and a body explaining *why*

questions.prompt: What is the primary goal of **code review** in open-source projects?

options.text: Approving every PR without reading it
Catching bugs, ensuring maintainability/test coverage, and sharing architectural knowledge
Nitpicking whitespace manually instead of using a formatter

questions.prompt: Which habits make a **pull request** easy for maintainers to review? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Including tests and explaining how the change was verified
Linking the related issue and noting any breaking changes
Bundling unrelated formatting changes across 80 files
Keeping the PR focused on one logical change

questions.prompt: What does **Semantic Versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`)** communicate?

options.text: `MAJOR`: breaking API changes, `MINOR`: backwards-compatible features, `PATCH`: backwards-compatible bug fixes

questions.prompt: When is a **Changelog (`CHANGELOG.md`)** most helpful to users?

options.text: When it lists every typo fix
When it groups Added, Changed, Deprecated, Fixed, and Security notes per release in human language

questions.prompt: What is a **CI (Continuous Integration)** pipeline?

options.text: Automated checks (lint, build, tests) triggered on every push or pull request

questions.prompt: Match each test layer to its primary scope.

columns.label: Verifies a single function or module in isolation with fast execution
Verifies interactions across modules, databases, or APIs
Verifies full user/CLI workflows against a realistic assembled system

questions.prompt: What does `git fetch upstream && git rebase upstream/main` do?

options.text: Fetches latest upstream commits and replays your local branch commits cleanly on top

code.source:
git fetch upstream
git rebase upstream/main

questions.prompt: What is a **Code of Conduct** in an open-source community?

options.text: A document setting behavioral expectations and reporting channels so contributors feel safe and respected

questions.prompt: Which items belong in a good **README.md**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: License and links to docs / contribution guide
Every internal unit test's source code
What the project does and who it is for
Quickstart installation and minimal working example

questions.prompt: Why should **security vulnerabilities** be reported privately via `SECURITY.md` rather than a public GitHub issue?

options.text: Security bugs cannot be fixed in Git
Public issues alert attackers to unpatched exploits before a fix and advisory are ready

questions.prompt: What is **issue triage**?

options.text: Reviewing incoming issues to verify reproducibility, add labels, request missing info, and prioritize

questions.prompt: What is **bus factor** in an open-source project?

options.text: The minimum number of key maintainers whose sudden absence would stall the project

questions.prompt: What does `git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Release v1.2.0"` create?

options.text: An annotated Git tag marking a specific release commit

code.source:
git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Release v1.2.0"
git push origin v1.2.0

questions.prompt: Which practices prevent **maintainer burnout**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Promising 24/7 free support SLA for every user question
Setting clear scope boundaries and saying 'no' politely to out-of-scope features
Automating formatting, linting, and release chores in CI
Delegating triage or module co-maintainership to trusted contributors

questions.prompt: What is **CalVer** (Calendar Versioning, e.g., `2026.11`)?

options.text: A versioning scheme based on release dates rather than strict breaking-change counters

questions.prompt: Why do projects use **issue templates** (bug report / feature request)?

options.text: To ensure reporters include version, OS, reproduction steps, and expected vs. actual behavior

questions.prompt: What is a **pre-release** tag like `v2.0.0-rc.1` in SemVer?

options.text: A version marked unstable / testing-only that is not yet the final `2.0.0` release

questions.prompt: Match each Git command to its purpose.

columns.label: Binary-searches commit history to pinpoint which commit introduced a bug
Applies a specific commit (e.g., a bugfix) onto another release branch
Creates a new commit that safely undoes a previous commit without rewriting shared history

questions.prompt: Why should you use `git revert` instead of `git reset --hard` + force-push on a shared `main` branch?

options.text: `git revert` preserves shared history by adding an inverse commit, avoiding breaking everyone else's clones

questions.prompt: What is a **deprecation warning**?

options.text: Immediately deleting a public API without notice
Announcing in docs and runtime/build warnings that an API will be removed in a future major version, with a migration path

questions.prompt: What is **good first issue** labeling for?

options.text: Highlighting well-scoped, self-contained tasks suitable for new contributors

questions.prompt: What does `git status --short` show?

options.text: Compact list of modified, staged, and untracked files in the working tree

questions.prompt: Which checks belong in a **CI workflow** for a library repository? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Automated unit and integration test suite

questions.prompt: What is **upstream** vs. **origin** in a forked Git setup?

options.text: `origin` is your personal fork; `upstream` is the original project repository

questions.prompt: What is **backporting** in release maintenance?

options.text: Applying a bug or security fix from `main` onto an older supported release branch (e.g., `v1.x`)

questions.prompt: Why do projects use **lockfiles** (`package-lock.json`, `Cargo.lock`, `poetry.lock`)?

options.text: To pin exact transitive dependency versions for reproducible builds and CI

questions.prompt: What does `git diff --staged` show?

options.text: Changes already added to the staging index ready for the next commit

questions.prompt: What is a **DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin)** (`Signed-off-by:`)?

options.text: A contributor attestation that they have the right to submit the code under the project's license

questions.prompt: Why should **code formatting** be enforced by automated tools (Prettier, Black, `gofmt`, `rustfmt`) rather than human reviewers?

options.text: Automated formatters eliminate subjective style debates and keep diffs focused on logic

questions.prompt: Which actions help **retain contributors** in an open-source project? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Clear documentation of architecture and test commands
Ignoring PRs for 6 months then closing them without comment

questions.prompt: What is **SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)**?

options.text: A machine-readable inventory of all dependencies and licenses included in a software release

questions.prompt: What is **squash merging** a PR?

options.text: Combining all noisy WIP commits from a PR branch into a single clean commit on `main`

questions.prompt: Why is **licensing compatibility** important when adding a third-party dependency?

options.text: A dependency's license (e.g., AGPL/GPL) can impose obligations on how your combined project is distributed

questions.prompt: What is an **LTS (Long-Term Support)** release?

options.text: A release branch guaranteed to receive security and critical bug fixes for an extended support window

questions.prompt: What is the hallmark of **healthy open-source stewardship**?

options.text: Balancing user needs, code quality, clear governance, automated CI/releases, and maintainer sustainability
